correctness.rationale: As abstract finite-word combinatorics, the endpoint restriction is exhaustive: the final-letter set is the involutive image of the first-letter set and must be disjoint from it. A singleton first-letter set allows at most nine words by the two-letter overlap test. For a two-letter first set the internally valid reversal-involution orbits are indivisible candidates, and pair conflicts encode both directions including all proper overlap lengths; the weight is the number of words. The frozen isolated-orbit and clique certificate gives 8+2+2+2+2+1=17. An independently written exhaustive subset enumeration, independent_enumeration.py, produced 6 usable orbits, optimum 7 and 2 maximizers for the singleton case; and 20 usable orbits, optimum 17 and 8 maximizers for the two-letter case. It checked the supplied witness and computed the group action on the transported codes: 32 labeled optima, four size-eight classes. Reversal acts on closed codes exactly as the letter involution. The frozen replay sources are verify.py with certificate.json and the standalone crosscheck.cpp, inspected but not executed. Nothing here verifies physical performance or other word lengths.
